title: Digit frequencies and class numbers
summary: Let $p>3$ be a prime and $b\ge 2$ an integer such that $p$ does not divide $b$. Then $1/p$ has a periodic digit expansion with respect to the basis $b$. The length $m$ of the period is the (multiplicative) order of $b$ mod $p$. In the case $m=(p-1)/2$, the frequency of each digit $k\in\{0,1,\ldots, b-1\}$ can be expressed in terms of generalized (first order) Bernoulli numbers. In some cases only Bernoulli numbers belonging to quadratic characters occur.
